content.evidence_note: Recipe actually used in §§4–8, not a new established Theorem. Imported random-matrix interfaces are read as stated in this PDF, not independently rederived from their external sources.
failure_modes: Conditioning the input prior on the spectral event destroys the stated unconditional Gaussian posterior argument.
A latent right rotation or enlarged sigma-field cannot be treated as algorithm-visible information.
Square-Wishart scalar estimation or matrix-game joint-matvec results do not directly imply this LRA claim.
Fixed-p overlap arguments cannot absorb growing p into universal constants.
content.goal_pattern: Control arbitrary measurable rank-k output projectors after adaptive products, then turn posterior uncertainty into relative Schatten error.
content.key_choice: Expose Gaussian row information using a transcript-measurable row basis and a latent right rotation. Enlarge the conditioning sigma-field only inside the proof so the remaining block stays independent Gaussian; use the tower property to return to the actual transcript.
content.key_relation: Lemma 4.1 leaves D_q of size (d−q)×(d−k−q) iid N(0,1/d). Theorem 4.6 gives E tr(P Pi_K)≤2k(q+k)/(d−q). Theorem 6.3 gives lambda_j^up(QWQ restricted to range(Q))≤C j²/[d(d−k−q)] simultaneously with conditional probability ≥0.95 for almost every transcript, for h=d−k−q≥1 and 1≤j≤h. If k+q≤d/2 this is C'j²/d². K=ker W; Q=I−P.
proof_skeleton: Orthogonalize informative symmetric-oracle queries. Lemma 4.1 uses G_{t+1}=G_t join sigma(z_t,b_t), b_t=D'_t u_t, while D' V_t remains independent Gaussian. No latent rotation is supplied to the algorithm.

For fixed finite p, bound the posterior bottom-block covariance by k/(d−q) times identity and the accumulated query-span nullspace mass by kq/(d−q). Markov bounds overlap ≥3k/4 by 0.1 when q,k are small fractions of d.

On Lemma 5.2's event of probability ≥0.95, H has spectrum in [1/2,1], top-k eigenspace K, and success forces k−tr(P Pi_K)≤C_p epsilon d³/k². Choose d≤eta_p k epsilon^(−1/3). Intersect events by a union bound, never by truncating the Gaussian prior.

For uniform p≥2 use S=I−H². Lemma 6.1 lower-bounds positive eigenvalues s_j by c(k+j)²/d². Theorem 6.3 upper-bounds the output compression eigenvalues theta_j by Cj²/d². Compare R_p=sum_j(1−theta_j)^(p/2) to Z_p=sum_j(1−s_j)^(p/2).

For large k, Lemmas 7.1–7.2 give Z_p≤Cd/sqrt(p), excess ≥c p k³/d² at bounded a²=pk²/d², and ratio ≥exp(ca²) at large a². For bounded k, Lemma 6.4 supplies a strict edge separation with unconditional probability >1/3, and Lemma 7.3 gives the corresponding one-mode comparison.

Use the rank baseline when R=O(k); otherwise d=floor(eta R), R=min(N,k Phi) or min(N,k/sqrt(epsilon)), q≤alpha d. Lemma 3.5 pads to rectangular dimensions. §8 compares with (1+epsilon)^p and applies Yao for the uniform result.
content.required_inputs: A fixed Gaussian factor X in R^{d×(d−k)} with iid N(0,1/d) entries; W=XX^T, H=I−W/L with public sufficiently large universal L. Exact symmetric matvec access, independent algorithm seed, standard Borel measurability and an all-path query cap. Lower-bound instance is sampled once, without conditioning its prior on a favourable spectral event.
transfer_obligations: Re-establish the Gaussian conditional-law interface if the prior or feedback changes.
Prove an information-to-error bridge for the actual output and loss; total overlap alone does not establish uniform-p performance.
Recalibrate bounded-rank probability to the requested confidence. Constant probability without a margin above 1/3 is insufficient here.
Recheck query units, padding and arbitrary output-subspace extraction; a block oracle charged once is different.
Retain the separate exact-rank branch, the dimension cap and the hierarchy of universal constants.
